title: THE ROLE OF ICT TOOLS IN PROMOTING LEARNER AUTONOMY
reason: ICT/LMS use and learner autonomy are both measured by survey and pre/post autonomy tests; no platform-recorded indicator. Results give no statistics at all (no coefficients, means or p-values).

extraction.design: mixed methods: pre/post quasi-experiment, survey correlation/regression, teacher interviews
extraction.n_quote: Approximately 200 students were chosen to participate in the quantitative aspect of the research.
extraction.population: first-year undergraduate EFL students, 1 public university; 20 teachers interviewed
extraction.lms_indicators: self-reported number and kind of ICT tools used (incl. LMS)
extraction.outcome_or_construct: learner autonomy (self-regulation, goal setting), SDT motivation
extraction.notes: Secondary E1: correlation, regression and ANOVA reported only verbally with no numbers; n given as 'approximately 200'.
